rationale: Tests core knowledge of direct vs indirect ophthalmoscopy optics — a frequent exam trap where students confuse image orientation and magnification.
Cup-to-disc ratio is a critical normal landmark; students must distinguish physiological cupping from glaucomatous cupping.
NPDR vs PDR distinction is the most critical clinical decision point in diabetic retinopathy — the defining feature being new vessel formation.
Management principle: systemic glycaemic and BP control is the foundation; students often underestimate its impact relative to laser or anti-VEGF.
CRAO vs CRVO is a classic exam trap — both cause sudden painless visual loss but have completely different fundoscopic pictures, mechanisms, and management.
Tests the time-critical nature of CRAO management — the 90-minute window mirrors acute stroke management and is frequently tested.
Retinoblastoma presenting as leukocoria is a life-threatening paediatric emergency; the key trap is misdiagnosis as refractive error or strabismus causing delayed referral.
Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment presenting with flashes and floaters — early recognition by non-specialists is critical to prevent macular involvement.
Differentiating papilloedema from optic neuritis and AION is a critical neuro-ophthalmology trap — they all cause disc swelling but have different laterality, pain, and associated features.
Bitemporal hemianopia localising to the optic chiasm is a foundational visual pathway anatomy question — relevant to pituitary tumour diagnosis.
